title: Rochdale MP seeks local role in pilot targeting repeat shoplifters
excerpt: Greater Manchester has been selected for a programme targeting repeat shop theft, but the locations have yet to be decided. Paul Waugh wants Rochdale included.
body:
Rochdale's town and district centres should be included in a new programme targeting repeat shoplifters, the town's MP has said, after Greater Manchester was selected to take part.

Paul Waugh's office said Policing and Crime Minister Sarah Jones had confirmed the force area's place in the Prolific Retail Offenders Pilot Programme in a letter this week. Local delivery plans are still being drawn up, and Rochdale has not yet been confirmed as a focus for the scheme.

The programme will bring police, probation, councils, housing and treatment services together with retailers to concentrate on people responsible for repeated shop theft. Alongside enforcement, it aims to address problems such as drug and alcohol misuse and unstable housing that can contribute to persistent offending.

Decisions about where work will be concentrated within Greater Manchester will be made locally, based on patterns of offending, according to the MP's office. No Rochdale start date, allocation of funding or number of people to be targeted was given in the release.

Mr Waugh said: "Shopkeepers and their staff in Rochdale tell me time and again that it is often the same faces coming back, week after week."

He said he would press local police and partners to include Rochdale's high streets and speak to retailers and business groups about their experience of repeat offending.

The Home Office's national announcement on 18 November said the programme would target around 500 prolific retail offenders across up to 16 police forces, with an initial £2.5 million available for participating forces and partners overall. That is a national funding pot, rather than an announced sum for Rochdale.

The National Police Chiefs' Council said the pilot would test a more intensive approach involving several agencies, with the aim of reducing repeat offending and improving outcomes for retailers and communities.

For Rochdale shop staff and businesses, the next decision is whether local centres are chosen for delivery. The MP's office has invited businesses to share their experiences with it.

Source: Office of Paul Waugh MP, press release issued on 18 November 2026; Home Office; National Police Chiefs' Council. Image: Rochdale Daily file photograph of police.
